dub_custom_clerk.text: Welcome to the Custom House. It was designed by James Gandon and finished in 1791. He also did the Four Courts, further up the river.
Look for the carved stone heads above the doors and windows. They represent Irish rivers, and one of them is the Atlantic Ocean.
The dome is topped by a statue of Commerce. I have never seen her do any.

dub_bureau.text: Welcome to Dublin port. Pounds into euros, euros into pounds, and a bit for ourselves in between.

dub_exchange.text: The Dublin board: Irish shares, priced in euros. The financial district grew up right here by the Custom House.

dub_auctioneer.text: Leases from the Enclosure's liquidation, by auction, in whichever currency the land prefers. Come and see the catalogue.

then.text: Off to mark essays. Somebody has dated the Treaty to 1066 again.

else.text: {greeting} I lecture in history across the river. I come here because this building has been through it.
It was burned in May 1921, in the War of Independence. That war came after the 1916 Rising, and ended with the Anglo-Irish Treaty that December.
The Irish Free State began on 6 December 1922. Six northern counties stayed in the UK as Northern Ireland. The Treaty split the country, and a civil war followed.
The 1937 constitution named the state Éire, or Ireland in English. In 1949 it became a republic and left the Commonwealth.
People say 'the Republic of Ireland' to tell the state from the island. Officially it's just Ireland. We're not fussy. Well, a bit.
And now? Neighbours. We joined the EEC on the same day as the UK, 1 January 1973. Then they left and we stayed. It's been a lot of meetings.
Noted in the Gazetteer, under How these isles work.
